The '''Golden Globe for New Star of the Year – Actress''' was an award presented by the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] (HFPA) at the annual [[Golden Globes]] award ceremony. New Star of the Year – Actress was first presented at the [[5th Golden Globes]] held in 1948, alongside the [[Golden Globe Award for New Star of the Year – Actor|New Star of the Year – Actor]] category, and awarded to [[Lois Maxwell]] for her performance in ''[[That Hagen Girl]]'' (1947); the award was absent from the following year's ceremony. From the [[7th Golden Globes]] onwards, New Star of the Year – Actress was presented in every ceremony—excluding the [[34th Golden Globes]]—until the [[40th Golden Globes]] held in 1983, with the final winner being [[Sandahl Bergman]] for ''[[Conan the Barbarian (1982 film)|Conan the Barbarian]]'' (1982).

The New Star of the Year – Actress award was presented 32 times, to 57 actresses. In 1951 and 1982, the award was merged with its male counterpart to create a unisex New Star of the Year category; the former was won by [[Gene Nelson]] for ''[[Tea for Two (film)|Tea for Two]]'' (1950) and the latter by [[Pia Zadora]] for ''[[Butterfly (1982 film)|Butterfly]]'' (1982). From the [[11th Golden Globes|11th]] to [[22nd Golden Globes]] the award was traditionally given to three actresses; starting with the [[23rd Golden Globes|23rd ceremony]], only one actress was declared the winner.

Zadora's 1982 win for ''Butterfly'' was viewed as "controversial", with the Golden Globes facing scrutiny over their decision.<ref name="THR">{{cite web |last1=Abramovitch |first1=Seth |title=Golden Globes: Pia Zadora Defends Controversial Win, Insists Ex-Husband "Did Not Buy" Award |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/golden-globes-pia-zadora-defends-761222/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=[[Eldridge Industries]] |access-date=July 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260522090140/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/golden-globes-pia-zadora-defends-761222/ |archive-date=May 22, 2026 |date=January 8, 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="LA Times">{{cite web |last1=Waxman |first1=Sharon |author1-link=Sharon Waxman |title=Hollywood Con Job |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-jan-11-oe-waxman11-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |publisher=Los Angeles Times Communications LLC |access-date=July 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714014826/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-jan-11-oe-waxman11-story.html |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |date=January 11, 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> Her husband and the producer of ''Butterfly'', Israeli businessman [[Meshulam Riklis]], had invited members of the HFPA over to the [[Riviera (hotel and casino)|Riviera]] — a hotel and casino he owned in [[Las Vegas]] — where he hosted them, treating them to wine and dinner;<ref name="LA Times"/><ref name="NY Times">{{cite web |last1=Sperling |first1=Nicole |last2=Barnes |first2=Brooks |title=How the Golden Globes Went From Laughingstock to Power Player |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/11/business/media/golden-globes-tom-cruise-nbc.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |publisher=[[The New York Times Company]] |access-date=July 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116010500/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/11/business/media/golden-globes-tom-cruise-nbc.html |archive-date=November 16, 2025 |date=May 11, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> at the hotel, Riklis employed Zadora as an entertainer and singer.<ref name="Newsday">{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Bill |title=Pia Zadora: Laughing All the Way |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/newsday-nassau-edition-pia-zadora-lau/204446905/ |access-date=August 23, 2026 |work=[[Newsday]]  |date=February 28, 1982 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823190000/https://www.newspapers.com/article/newsday-nassau-edition-pia-zadora-lau/204446905/ |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |location=[[Hempstead, New York]], [[United States]] |page=91 |via=[[Ancestry.com#Newspapers.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live}} {{free access}}</ref><ref name="Herald-Sun">{{cite news |last=Wilson |first=Earl |title=Pia a Controversial Figure |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-herald-sun-pia-a-controversial-figur/204446645/ |access-date=August 23, 2026 |work=[[The Herald-Sun (Durham, North Carolina)|The Herald-Sun]] |date=February 15, 1982 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823191529/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-herald-sun-pia-a-controversial-figur/204446645/ |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |location=[[Durham, North Carolina]], [[United States]] |page=20 |via=[[Ancestry.com#Newspapers.com|Newspapers.com]] |url-status=live}} {{free access}}</ref> While at the Riviera, the HFPA members were also shown a private screening of ''Butterfly'' and saw Zadora perform her [[nightclub act]].<ref name="THR"/><ref name="Newsday" /><ref name="People">{{cite web |last1=Adelson |first1=Suzanne |last2=Marx |first2=Linda |title=How Did Actress Pia Zadora Ever Win a Golden Globe? The Answer Is Riklis Love |url=http://www.people.com/people/archive/article/0%2C%2C20081499%2C00.html |website=[[People (magazine)|People]] |publisher=[[People Inc.]] |access-date=July 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101219231639/http://www.people.com/people/archive/article/0,,20081499,00.html |archive-date=December 19, 2010 |date=February 22, 1982 |url-status=dead}}</ref>{{efn|According to an article from the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', written by Aljean Harmetz in 2000, the HFPA members were flown over to Las Vegas by [[New Frontier Hotel and Casino]], to watch the animal-based magic show [[Siegfried & Roy]]; Riklis only provided a single night's free lodging to them while there.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Harmetz |first1=Aljean |title=As the Golden Globes Turn |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jan-23-ca-56604-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |publisher=Los Angeles Times Communications LLC |access-date=August 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823213101/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jan-23-ca-56604-story.html |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |date=January 23, 2000 |url-status=live}}</ref>}} Six weeks later, Riklis invited another group to his and Zadora's home in [[Beverly Hills]] for one more private screening of the film.<ref name="THR"/><ref name="People"/> It was presumed that Riklis had bought the award for Zadora; after the following year's ceremony, the New Star of the Year awards were discontinued by the Golden Globes.<ref name="THR" /><ref name="Newsday"/>

[[Pat Crowley]], [[Bella Darvi]], and [[Carroll Baker]] are the only actresses to have received the award for two separate performances in the same ceremony; Crowley won for ''[[Forever Female]]'' and ''[[Money from Home]]'', Darvi for ''[[The Egyptian (film)|The Egyptian]]'' and ''[[Hell and High Water (1954 film)|Hell and High Water]]'', and Baker for ''[[Baby Doll]]'' and ''[[Giant (1956 film)|Giant]]''. [[Carol Lynley]] was the only actress to be nominated twice in two separate ceremonies; first in 1959 for ''[[The Light in the Forest (film)|The Light in the Forest]]'' and then again the following year for ''[[Blue Denim]]''.
